title: Firm and Unmov'd Are They
description: Firm and Unmov'd Are They in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 125, part 2, headed “The saints' trial and safety; or, Moderated afflictions”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Firm and un-mov'd are they That rest their souls on God; Firm as the mount where Da-vid dwelt Or where the ark a-bode.

lines: That rest their souls on God;
Firm as the mount where David dwelt
So God and his almighty love
Yet, lest it wound their souls too deep,
Whose hope, and love, and every grace
The God of Israel will support
Will chuse the road to hell,
We must expect our portion there

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
